campaign_name: Initiatives to the 2027 Legislature (IL27 cycle) - none verified collecting
purpose: Initiatives to the Legislature filed in 2026 that would go to the 2027 session
type: Initiative to the Legislature (indirect statutory initiative)
evidence_note: The WA SOS page confirms a 308,911-signature threshold and a Dec 31, 2026 deadline for initiatives to the Legislature, but the fetched page did not render the list of filings. Searches found no news of any IL27-numbered measure collecting signatures. In May 2026 Let's Go Washington called a 2027 initiative to the Legislature its 'second option' for the income-tax repeal, but it took the 2026 ballot route instead (I-645, already recorded; 511,408 signatures filed July 2, 2026). Check the SOS list directly for current IL27 filings.

campaign_name: Let's Go Washington - signature firm spending benchmark (Allstate Petition Management)
purpose: Benchmark for paid-firm costs on WA initiatives to the Legislature (2023 six-initiative drive)
circulation_firm: Allstate Petition Management (APM), plus a second unnamed firm
budget_or_spend: $1.9 million reported paid to APM (per PDC charges reported Sept 2024)
evidence_note: In 2024, PDC staff charged LGW with inaccurate and late reporting of signature-gathering spending and with failing to collect vendor subcontractor spending information. LGW reported $1.9M paid to APM for six 2023 initiatives (three were adopted by the Legislature). This is historical, but it shows LGW pays a firm and what that costs. No 2026-cycle PDC firm payments were verified in this pass.

purpose: Constitutional amendment repealing Prop 14's top-two primary; targets the Nov 2028 ballot
sponsor: Steven Maviglio (proponent; Forza Communications); endorsed by Ron Nehring; Carl DeMaio / Reform California pledged funding and volunteers; Lorena Gonzalez (CA Labor Fed) said unions 'likely support'
budget_or_spend: unknown (no committee appeared on FPPC pending/circulating top-contributor lists checked)
contact: steven.maviglio@gmail.com (proponent contact listed in CA SOS release PR26-103)
evidence_note: Cleared for circulation July 2026, with signatures due to counties by Jan 11, 2027. DeMaio claimed 18,000 volunteer gatherers (source: IVP, which opposes the measure). No signature firm, Cal-Access committee spending or paid-gatherer ads were found. The opposition committee, More Choice California, is funded mainly by the Independent Voter Project. Reaching 874k valid signatures in 6 months usually takes paid circulation, but that is not confirmed. Cal-Access was not searched directly.

purpose: Bar transgender girls from girls' school sports divisions
sponsor: Protect Girls' Sports PAC (backed by Gov. Joe Lombardo)

evidence_note: Lombardo dropped the 2026 petition despite winning in the NV Supreme Court on June 18, citing legal delays. He asked the 2027 Legislature to act and vowed to bring the petition back if it doesn't. No current signature collection was found.

campaign_name: Vote Nevada PAC - redistricting / Voters' Bill of Rights / unfunded-mandate fix / digital signatures
purpose: Nonpartisan redistricting, open primaries, and initiative-process reforms
type: Initiative constitutional amendments and a statutory initiative
sponsor: Vote Nevada PAC (Sondra Cosgrove, Doug Goodman)
budget_or_spend: No funding disclosures as of Oct 2025; lacked funds to appeal court losses
evidence_note: Volunteers could not gather enough physical signatures, a judge struck the redistricting measure as an unfunded mandate, and the digital-signature measure was withdrawn after a challenge from BizPAC. This is a funded-infrastructure gap: the group may refile for 2028 (not announced). Only 2 statewide questions (Q6, Q7, both legislative second votes) are on NV's Nov 2026 ballot. No 2028 initiative filings or active county/city petitions or recalls were verified. The recalls found were 2020 or older.

campaign_name: County charter petitions or recalls - none verified
evidence_note: Hawaii's 2026 county charter questions (Honolulu 20, Maui 8, Hawaii County) come from charter commissions or councils, not citizen petitions. Maui Charter Question 2 would standardize clerk deadlines for processing initiative, recall and charter petitions (procedural only). No active recall found.
